questions.q: Imagine a new planet having the same density as that of the earth, but it is two times bigger than the earth in size. If the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the new planet is g' and that on the surface of the earth is g, then
questions.explanation: $g=\dfrac{GM}{R^2}=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi G\rho R$, so for the same density, g ∝ R. With R doubled, g' = 2g.

questions.q: Suppose the acceleration due to gravity at the earth's surface is g m/s$^2$ and at the surface of moon it is g' m/s$^2$. An M kg passenger goes from the earth to the moon in a spaceship moving with a constant velocity (Neglect all other objects in the sky). Which curve best represents the weight (net gravitational force) as a function of time? [Figure: weight vs time graph with four curves A, B, C, D all starting at Mg (t=0) and ending at Mg' (t=t$_0$); curve A falls off gradually and smoothly; curve B is close to a straight line; curves C and D dip well below Mg' in the middle before rising back up to Mg' at t$_0$, with C dipping less than D]
questions.explanation: As the spaceship moves away from Earth, Earth's pull (∝1/r²) falls off quickly while the Moon's pull stays small until the ship is close to the Moon, so the net weight dips below Mg' in the middle of the journey before rising back to Mg' at the Moon's surface — the shape of curve C.

questions.q: If r$_p$, v$_p$, L$_p$ and r$_a$, v$_a$, L$_a$ are radii, velocities and angular momenta of a planet at perihelion and aphelion of its elliptical orbit around the Sun respectively, then
questions.explanation: Perihelion is the closest point (smaller r, larger v by Kepler's law of areas), and angular momentum about the Sun is conserved throughout the orbit, so $L_a=L_p$.

questions.q: The total energy of a satellite in a circular orbit at a distance (R + h) from the center of the Earth varies as [R is the radius of the Earth and h is the height of the orbit from Earth's surface]
questions.explanation: Total energy of an orbiting satellite is $E=-\dfrac{GMm}{2(R+h)}$, which varies as $-1/(R+h)$.

questions.q: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to half the radius of the Earth, from its surface?
When a planet revolves around the Sun, in general, for the planet
options: linear momentum and aerial velocity are constant.
kinetic and potential energy of the planet are constant.
angular momentum about the Sun and aerial velocity of the planet are constant.
linear momentum and linear velocity are constant.
questions.explanation: Since gravity is a central force, angular momentum about the Sun is conserved, and by Kepler's second law the areal velocity is constant.

questions.q: Two bodies of masses 8 kg are placed at the vertices A and B of an equilateral triangle ABC. A third body of mass 2 kg is placed at the centroid G of the triangle. If AG = BG = CG = 1 m, where should a fourth body of mass 4 kg be placed so that the resultant force on the 2 kg body is zero?
options: at a point P on the line CG such that PG = $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ m
at a point P on the line CG such that PG = 0.5 m
at a point P on the line CG such that PG = 2m
questions.explanation: The resultant gravitational pull of the two 8 kg masses on the 2 kg mass (angle AGB = 120°) has magnitude $G\cdot16\cdot2$ directed away from C. Setting the 4 kg mass's pull $\dfrac{G\cdot4\cdot2}{d^2}$ equal to this gives $d=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ m along CG.

questions.q: The value of acceleration due to gravity at a height of 10 km from the surface of earth is x. At what depth inside the earth is the value of the acceleration due to gravity has the same value x?
questions.explanation: For small heights/depths, $g_h=g(1-2h/R)$ and $g_d=g(1-d/R)$; equating gives $d=2h=20$ km.

questions.q: A satellite is orbiting close to the earth and has a kinetic energy K. The minimum extra kinetic energy required by it to just overcome the gravitation pull of the earth is
questions.explanation: For a satellite in a close orbit, total energy $= -K$ (since KE = $|PE|/2$); to escape, total energy must become zero, so extra kinetic energy needed is K.

questions.q: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of 'g' on the Earth?
options: g rises linearly to a peak at r = R then falls
g rises to a peak at r = R then falls off as a curve
g rises linearly to r = R and stays constant beyond
g stays constant up to r = R then falls off as a curve
questions.explanation: Inside the Earth g increases linearly with distance from the centre (g = g_s r/R), reaches a maximum at the surface r = R, and decreases as 1/r² outside — matching option (B).

questions.q: A mass 'm' on the surface of the Earth is shifted to a target equal to the radius of the Earth. If 'R' is the radius and 'M' is the mass of the Earth, then work done in this process is
questions.explanation: Work done to move a mass from the Earth's surface (r = R) to r = 2R is W = GMm(1/R − 1/2R) = GMm/2R = mgR/2, since g = GM/R².

questions.q: A space station is at a height equal to the radius of the Earth. If '$v_E$' is the escape velocity on the surface of the Earth, the same on the space station is ____ times $v_E$.
questions.explanation: Escape velocity at distance 2R from the centre: v' = $\sqrt{2GM/2R}$ = $\sqrt{GM/R}$ = $v_E$/$\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: The value of acceleration due to gravity at a depth of 1600 km is equal to [Radius of earth = 6400 km]
questions.explanation: $g_d = g\left(1 - \dfrac{d}{R}\right) = 9.8 \left(1 - \dfrac{1600}{6400}\right) = 9.8 \times 0.75 = 7.35$ ms$^{-2}$.

questions.q: Variation of acceleration due to gravity (g) with distance x from the centre of the earth is best represented by (R -> Radius of the earth)
options: g decreases from a high value at x = 0 down to a minimum at x = R, then increases with x
g increases linearly from 0 at x = 0 up to x = R, then keeps increasing beyond R
g is high at x = 0 and decreases continuously (monotonically) through x = R and beyond
g increases linearly from 0 at x = 0 to a maximum at x = R, then decreases (as $1/x^2$) for x > R
questions.explanation: Inside the earth $g \propto x$ (rises linearly from 0 at the centre), and outside $g \propto 1/x^2$ (falls off), so g peaks at x = R.

questions.q: If the mass of a body is M on the surface of the earth, the mass of the same body on the surface of the moon is
questions.explanation: Mass is an intrinsic property independent of the local gravitational field; only the weight changes on the moon, so the mass remains M.

questions.q: What is a period of revolution of earth satellite? Ignore the height of satellite above the surface of earth. Given: (1) The value of gravitational acceleration g = 10 ms$^{-2}$. (2) Radius of earth R$_E$ = 6400 km. Take $\pi$ = 3.14.
questions.explanation: T = 2$\pi\sqrt{R/g}$ = 2\times3.14\times\sqrt{6.4\times10^6/10} = 2\times3.14\times800 = 5024 s = 83.73 minutes.

questions.q: A period of geostationary satellite is
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite has the same period as Earth's rotation, 24 hours.

questions.q: Earth is moving around the Sun in elliptical orbit as shown. The ratio of OB and OA is R. Then the ratio of speed of Earth at A and B is [an ellipse with the Sun at its centre O; A is the topmost point (end of the minor axis) and B is the rightmost point (end of the major axis); OB/OA = R]
questions.explanation: By conservation of angular momentum (areal velocity) about O, speed is inversely proportional to distance from O, so the ratio of speeds at A and B equals OB:OA = R. KEA awarded grace marks for this question, likely because of the ambiguous figure (the Sun should really be at a focus, not the centre, of the ellipse).

questions.q: A planet moving around sun sweeps area A$_1$ in 2 days, A$_2$ in 3 days and A$_3$ in 6 days [figure: sun with three sectors of areas A$_1$, A$_2$, A$_3$ swept out from the sun]. Then the relation between A$_1$, A$_2$ and A$_3$ is
questions.explanation: By Kepler's second law the areal velocity is constant, so A$_1$/2 = A$_2$/3 = A$_3$/6; multiplying through by 6 gives 3A$_1$ = 2A$_2$ = A$_3$.

questions.q: Two satellites of mass $m$ and $9m$ are orbiting a planet in orbits of radius $R$. Their periods of revolution will be in the ratio of .................
questions.explanation: The orbital period $T=2\pi\sqrt{R^3/GM}$ depends only on the orbit radius $R$ and the planet's mass, not on the satellite's mass, so the ratio is $1:1$.

questions.q: An astronaut on a strange planet finds that acceleration due to gravity is twice as that on the surface of Earth. Which of the following could explain this?
options: Both the mass and radius of the planet are twice as that of Earth.
Mass of the planet is half as that of Earth, but radius is same as that of Earth.
Both the mass and radius of the planet are half as that of Earth.
Radius of the planet is half as that of Earth, but the mass is the same as that of Earth.
questions.explanation: $g=GM/R^2$; halving both $M$ and $R$ gives $g'=G(M/2)/(R/2)^2=2GM/R^2=2g$.

questions.q: A planet revolves round the Sun in an elliptical orbit [A and C are the ends of the major axis, with the Sun shown offset towards A; B and D are the ends of the minor axis]. The linear speed of the planet will be maximum at
questions.explanation: By Kepler's second law (conservation of angular momentum), the planet moves fastest at perihelion, the point closest to the Sun, which is A.
